extracted.intended_audience: EPA stakeholders (regulated industry, environmental organizations, policymakers), legal practitioners, and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: Official EPA findings under Clean Air Act section 202(a) determining (1) whether concentrations of specified greenhouse gases endanger public health or welfare and (2) whether emissions from new motor vehicles/engines (and separately aircraft) cause or contribute to that pollution. The page summarizes the findings, supporting technical evidence, procedural history, and post-rule challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endangerment Finding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator finds that the current and projected concentrations of the six key well-mixed greenhouse gases—carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), perfluorocarbons (PFCs), and sulfur hexafluoride (SF6)—in the atmosphere threaten the public health and welfare of current and future generations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the substantive determination that greenhouse gas concentrations pose a threat to public health and welfare. The EPA documents scientific and technical information supporting this conclusion in the Technical Support Document for the Findings and addresses public comments in its Response to Comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause or Contribute Finding (new motor vehicles/engines)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator finds that the combined emissions of these well-mixed greenhouse gases from new motor vehicles and new motor vehicle engines contribute to the greenhouse gas pollution that threatens public health and welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This finding links vehicle emissions to the identified endangerment and served as a prerequisite for implementing greenhouse gas emissions standards for vehicles and other sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate Aircraft Cause or Contribute Finding
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate finding was made regarding greenhouse gas emissions from aircraft: Final Rule for Finding That Greenhouse Gas Emissions From Aircraft Cause or Contribute to Air Pollution That May Reasonably Be Anticipated to Endanger Public Health and Welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aircraft emissions were addressed in a distinct rulemaking; see the cited final rule for specifics. The aircraft finding follows the same cause-or-contribute framing as the vehicle finding but applies to aircraft sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator decision standard from Massachusetts v. EPA
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court held that the Administrator must determine whether or not emissions of greenhouse gases from new motor vehicles cause or contribute to air pollution that may reasonably be anticipated to endanger public health or welfare, or whether the science is too uncertain to make a reasoned decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This articulates the legal standard the Administrator must apply: make a reasoned determination either that emissions cause/contribute to endangerment or that scientific uncertainty precludes such a determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to follow Section 202(a) statutory language
rubrics_metrics.description: In making these decisions, the Administrator is required to follow the language of section 202(a) of the Clean Air Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions must be framed and justified according to the statutory text of CAA §202(a); legal adherence to the statute is a governing constraint on the factual/technical determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standard: reliance on scientific and technical information
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific and technical information summarized to support the Endangerment and Cause or Contribute Findings for Greenhouse Gases under the Clean Air Act can be found in the Technical Support Document for the Findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA relied on a Technical Support Document and a formal public comment process (a 60‑day comment period with over 380,000 comments, including hearings) — EPA 'carefully reviewed, considered, and incorporated public comments' when issuing the final Findings. The TSD and Response to Comments constitute the evidentiary and deliberative record supporting the findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural effect and publication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: These findings do not themselves impose any requirements on industry or other entities. However, this action was a prerequisite for implementing greenhouse gas emissions standards for vehicles and other sectors. The final rule was published in the Federal Register under Docket ID No. EPA-HQ-OAR-2009-0171 and was effective January 14, 2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page indicates the procedural consequence of the findings (enabling subsequent standards) and provides citation/publication details (Federal Register docket and effective date) that are part of the formal rulemaking record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑rule administrative and judicial review history
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA denied ten Petitions Received in 2009-2010 for Reconsideration on July 29, 2010; denied four Petitions Received in 2017-2019 for Reconsideration, Rulemaking, or Reopening on April 21, 2022; and the U.S. Court of Appeals–D.C. Circuit on June 26, 2012, decided to uphold EPA's GHG Endangerment and Cause or Contribute Findings and related regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page summarizes the administrative petition and judicial review posture of the findings — indicating the standard of review and that EPA's determinations have been litigated and judicially upheld. This informs stakeholders about the stability and reviewability of the determinations.
